title: How Jobs explained Apple's edge at D5 2007: software in beautiful hardware, argued ideas, recruiting
summary: At D5 in 2007, Jobs explains why the iPod and iPhone win: they are software wrapped in beautiful hardware, built by bright people who argue about ideas. He also covers framing Apple TV as a DVD player for the internet, dropping the physical keyboard, and building tools that surprise you.

principles.text: Great products are software wrapped in beautiful hardware; competitors can copy hardware but not software.
principles.quote: It's software wrapped in a beautiful package. And the Japanese consumer electronics companies couldn't make the leap to create that kind of software.

principles.text: To hire and keep bright people, you can't tell them what to do; run on arguing about ideas.
principles.quote: If you want to, if you want to hire and keep really bright people, then you can't tell them what to do.

principles.text: Recruiting is the heart and soul of the company when your only asset is ideas and people.
principles.quote: all we are is our ideas, which means all we are is our people.

principles.text: Choose a go-to-market path you can actually own; don't replace the set top box, be a DVD player for the internet.
principles.quote: We didn't do it because we couldn't see a go to market strategy that made sense.

principles.text: A touch screen beats a physical keyboard because the interface can change with new ideas and applications.
principles.quote: you can keep changing the user interface as you come up with new ideas, new applications.

principles.text: Make tools for people and stay open to being surprised by what they do with them.
principles.quote: we make these tools and they're constantly surprising us in new ways, what we can do with them.
